construct.constructDefinition: Digital resources: teacher self-positioning on digital-competence maturity statements. Preserves each competence’s A1–C2 statement and separate zero-point not-aware response; not an agreement scale, a teaching-quality measure or an observed performance test. No area/global aggregate is computed by this split unit.

population.populationNotes: Adult primary and secondary teachers able to understand the fixed English Toolkit. Initial digital split scope; age18+ is a project scope, not a source-derived validation cut-off. Source studies do not establish Chinese-language or separate-area digital equivalence. Early-years use on the current website is not borrowed as validation for this fixed primary/secondary version.

administration.timeFrame: Current professional digital practice and experience; no fixed day/week recall period.
layoutConstraints: Choose the ONE original maturity statement that best describes your current competence in each item. Six item-specific A1/A2/B1/B2/C1/C2 statements are scored1–6, and the seventh not-aware response is scored0.
Keep the original competence order and original option order; no agreement anchors, automatic reversal, simplified alternatives or shortened items.
Six separate native area units are project packaging; independent administration equivalence is not established. The ordinary-composite recipe retains all32 competences in order.
This unit reports each competence separately; no area mean, global192-point total or overall A1–C2 band is manufactured across the split tools.

Missing items remain null; 0 is a real not-aware answer, not missing data. Any unanswered competence makes this area incomplete and suppresses its interpretations; this complete-area policy is a project choice, not an inferred source missing-data algorithm.
Timing is an approximate project allocation of the official circa25-minute whole-tool estimate, not measured timing.

intendedUses.notes: Professional learning self-reflection using a fixed EU source, not a certification, teacher appraisal or observed competence test.
Separate-area digital packaging and local applicability require explicit interpretation limits; not automatic cross-language/role equivalence.

options.label: A1: I am aware that I can search for resources online (e.g. using a search engine, following a link, visiting a resource repository).
A2: I have tried searching online to find digital resources (e.g. by following a link, using key words in a search engine, filtering resources in online repositories).

B1: I use various online tools and portals to search for a wide and diversified set of digital resources that respond to educational needs (e.g. annotated selection of resources, search engines, resource repositories, digital libraries, social networks, learning communities).
B2: I analyse and select digital resources based on criteria that meet specific teaching and learning aims (e.g. pedagogical value, relevance, reliability, validity, quality, licensing).

C1: I reflect on my search results and readjust my selection criteria (e.g. taking into consideration that my search results can be affected by my geographical location or previous searches and preferences).

C2: I propose strategies and tools to help colleagues search for and select digital resources from diverse sources in line with curriculum requirements and learning aims (e.g. pools of key words, selection checklists, digital resources evaluation rubrics, references to resources portals).
I am not aware of this competence.
A1: I am aware that I can create resources in digital form (e.g. digital text, images, photos, audio, video).
A2: I have tried using digital tools to create resources (e.g. text editors, audio and visual editing tools, multimedia authoring tools).

B1: I use various digital tools according to their features to create digital resources to meet learners’ needs (e.g. interactive text, multimedia presentations, quizzes, games, online activities and lessons).
B2: I apply design principles and processes to create digital resources to meet teaching and learning aims (e.g. identifying a need, design, develop, implement, assess, adjust, share).

C1: I share the digital resources I create and I reflect and readjust them according to feedback that I receive (e.g. incorporating learner-centered pedagogical approaches enhanced by digital technologies affordances).

C2: I initiate and contribute to the co-creation of digital educational resources with people and organisations beyond my school (e.g. researchers, educational content publishers, educational technology companies).
I am not aware of this competence.

A1: I am aware that when modifying existing digital resources I need to respect copyright and licencing rules (e.g. adding a picture to text, adding new content, editing or deleting parts, adding hyperlinks).

A2: I have tried ways to modify existing digital resources, while respecting their copyright and licence attributes (e.g. editing a presentation, modifying an image, changing format of a video, editing quizzes, adapting general settings).

B1: I use various digital tools based on their features to modify and repurpose digital resources to meet educational needs (e.g. customise content of an online lesson, exploit features of a virtual environment, use eBook editors).

B2: I select existing digital resources, taking into consideration copyright and distribution licences, to modify and adapt them to meet teaching and learning aims (e.g. open educational resources, content under Creative Common License, content free of copyright, editable resources).

C1: I reflect on and redesign existing digital reources to integrate them into interactive, learner-centred activities (e.g. adapting digital resources and digitally-enhanced tasks into an online learning course, online assessment, online collaborative project, a wiki, a blog, a virtual learning space).

C2: I initiate and contribute to school-level guidance for teachers and students on modifying existing digital resources in line with curriculum requirements and teaching and learning aims (e.g. strategies to revise, improve and repurpose school’s digital resources, copyright licences to be used, agreements with external stakeholders and publishers).
I am not aware of this competence.

A1: I am aware that digital technologies can help me store, organise, and provide secure access to digital content (e.g. local and online storage spaces, password protection, classification of content).
A2: I have tried ways to store, manage and access digital content on and from local and/or online storage spaces (e.g. hard disks, external drives, cloud, online services).
B1: I use various digital tools to store, organise and facilitate access to digital content (e.g. tree structures, use of metadata/tags).

B2: I define and apply protection and security measures for the storage, management and access of digital content (e.g. applying strong passwords to sensitive content, assigning access limitation rights, use encryption protocols, have regular backups, select storage and online services based on their data policy, terms of use, safety and security).

C1: I design and develop a strategy to ensure easy, equitable and secure management of and access to digital content for my students and colleagues (e.g. classification of content, access limitation rights to different target users, encryption protocols, regular backups).

C2: I initiate and promote a common digital space at school-level, that facilitates the secure storage, management of and access to digital content for different targeted users (e.g. students, parents, teachers, other school staff).
I am not aware of this competence.
A1: I am aware that copyright rules apply to digital resources I use for educational purposes (e.g. images, text, audio, video).
A2: I have tried ways to attribute to the creator of the resources I use (e.g. citing author’s name, link to original source).

B1: I share digital resources attributing the original creators and choosing the most appropriate channels for private, limited or public use (e.g. using email attachment for private and limited use, through a link, in an online repository, a social network, managing tags/metadata).
B2: I select and apply copyright licences when sharing digital resources I create, supporting open educational resources (e.g. Creative Commons licence).

C1: I design and develop ways for my colleagues and I to share, curate and re-use digital resources to ensure easy and equal access (e.g. developing an ontology to manage resources, specifying ways to curate content, contextualising curated content).

C2: I initiate and promote an online space to share digital educational resources with the school community (e.g. applying key words /tags/metadata, allowing others to comment, rate, modify, or co-create).
I am not aware of this competence.

items.content: 2.1. Digital Resources- Searching and selecting Using searching and selection criteria to identify digital resources for teaching and learning.
2.2. Digital Resources - Creating Creating digital resources that support and enhance teaching and learning aims.
2.3. Digital Resources – Modifying Modifying existing digital resources to support and enhance teaching and learning aims, respecting copyright and licencing rules.
2.4. Digital Resources – Managing and protecting Organising digital content, enabling easy and secure access for students, parents and teachers, while protecting sensitive and personal data.
2.5. Digital Resources – Sharing Sharing digital content with respect to intellectual property and copyright rules.

interpretations.headline: Reflecting on competence 2.1
interpretations.summary: This response records the maturity statement you selected for this specific digital competence. The statements describe awareness, exploration, use, purposeful selection, reflective support and wider initiative in item-specific ways. A higher point value indicates a later self-described position in this framework; it does not establish better teaching or better student outcomes. The separate not-aware response is a valid starting point for learning. Use a recent example and your working conditions to put the choice in context. The displayed points preserve the original statement order: 0 = not aware; 1 = A1; 2 = A2; 3 = B1; 4 = B2; 5 = C1; 6 = C2. These codes are maturity statements within this framework, not agreement levels, teacher grades or population percentiles.

guidance.text: Choose one recent example connected with this competence. What did you do, what evidence did you notice, and which conditions helped or limited it?

limitations: Fixed source: 2022 Toolkit Annex I for complete item text and A1–C2 labels; official2023 report p.11/Annex1 for seventh not-aware option and0–6 point mapping. The2023 report omits the B2 row for6.5; no omitted row was invented.
These are self-reported digital-competence positions, not observed teaching, student learning outcomes, professional certification, personality labels or a school/teacher ranking.

The six separate digital area units, instructions, feedback and conservative missing policy are project adaptations. Current online text, independent-area validity and Chinese-version validity were not established.

Missing answers remain null and are not treated as a zero-point not-aware response. Any missing competence makes this area invalid/incomplete for interpretation. Other area units have their own completeness; no missing value is imputed. This project policy is not claimed as an author-issued missing-data algorithm.

No area average, global192-point score, overall proficiency band, population norm, percentile or cross-tool total is supplied. Consult the official Toolkit and2023 report for original glossary and full-tool interpretation.
report.disclaimer: For supportive professional learning reflection by the teacher receiving their own authorized results. A1–C2 are this framework’s maturity codes, not grades for teacher quality. No EU endorsement, badge or certificate is issued. Existing access and feedback permissions still apply.

instruction.text: Reflect on your current professional digital practice. For each competence choose the ONE statement that best describes your current position. A1, A2, B1, B2, C1 and C2 are progressive, item-specific statements; they are not agreement ratings. If appropriate, choose “I am not aware of this competence”, which is a real zero-point answer. A missing response remains missing. This digital unit is one area of the fixed2022 SELFIEforTEACHERS Toolkit and uses the official per-item0–6 mapping described in2023. Feedback is for your professional learning, not teacher appraisal, EU certification or student-outcome prediction.
instruction.source: Project-written digital instruction grounded in JRC129699 Toolkit self-reflection navigation/AnnexI and JRC131282 p.11/Annex1; not a verbatim official platform instruction.
